# A function reading a context, taken as a value where a provider is in
# scope, is a lambda passing the provided value (passContext's
# funcValueUnder). Its parameters kept the function's own names, so spliced
# into a component with a prop of one of them -- an openapi: adapter's `id`
# beside petRetrieveCall's `id` -- the lambda read the prop for its
# argument: here `pick(name="b")` answered "b!" for every key. Under a loop
# the prop was the loop variable, and the effect calling the lambda refused
# a read of a loop variable it does not run inside.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

context #suffix("?")

func shout(name string, life async.Lifetime) async.Result[string] {
    return {ok=name + suffix}
}

component pick(name string) ui.node {
    var answer option[string] = null
    async.query(on="key", fetch=shout, :value=answer)
    ui.text(value=answer != null ? answer : name)
}

component one ui.node {
    suffix("!") {
        pick #p(name="b")
    }
}

component rows ui.node {
    var names = ["x", "y"]
    suffix("!") {
        for var n = names {
            pick #r(name=n)
        }
    }
}

func testTheArgumentIsTheKey(t test.Test, c one) {
    t.wait(func() => c.p.answer != null, 2000)
    t.assert(c.p.answer == "key!")
}

func testEachCopyAsksWithItsKey(t test.Test, c rows) {
    t.wait(func() => c.r[1].answer != null, 2000)
    t.assert(c.r[1].answer == "key!")
}

ui.window {
    one()
    rows()
}
